subject: Re: Post-call recap & Redwood-verified benchmarks — Acme model fit
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@acmecorp.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit / evals

Hi Mike / Sara —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Key goals you mentioned: summarize user intents at scale, reranking short answers, and sub-200ms p50 latency for 512-token sessions.
- Data: you’re comfortable sharing a ~2k prompt-set subset (anonymized) for model-fit benchmarking.
- Success criteria: >= 92% quality pass on your eval rubric for intent classification, and latency p95 <= 400ms on a single-region deployment.

What we’ll do (next 72 hours):
1) Run Redwood’s model-fit evals across 3 recommended variants: an Llama-3 13B quantized profile, a Mistral-7B-v2 float, and a Redwood-optimized 70B distilled variant.
2) Share Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS, latency percentiles, memory footprint) and a short report with links to raw benchmark results.
3) Return prompt-set-specific quality regression notes and suggestions (prompt templates / guardrails) where we spot regressions.

Deliverables I’ll share in the next email: benchmark links, a PDF with verified profiles, and the anonymized prompt-set we used (we’ll also attach the acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl).

Proposed follow-up: 30 minutes next Tue (2026-03-09) to review findings and mutual action plan. Is that good on your side?

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Alex —

Appreciate the succinct recap. That aligns with our thinking. Two quick clarifications: 

1) For the latency SLA we care most about p95 for interactive UI flows (target <= 400ms). p50 is great for baseline.
2) We’ll upload the anonymized prompt-set to the S3 share you provided this afternoon and cc the Benchmarks Team. Expect it by EOD tomorrow.

Yes to the 3 candidate models — please include any recommended quantization points if you think they materially change quality.

Catch you soon,
Mike
CTO, Acme Corp
mike.johnson@acmecorp.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Johnson <mike.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Benchmarks Team <benchmarks@evals.io>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit / evals

Hi Mike / Benchmarks Team —

Thanks for confirming. We pulled the anonymized prompt-set and ran the first-pass model-fit evals overnight. High-level summary below, full links and PDF attached.

High-level recommendations (short):
- For your mix of short intents + occasional long context, we recommend starting with Mistral-7B-v2 (float) for best cost/quality tradeoff and Llama-3-13B (INT4 quantized) as a low-cost fallback where p95 latency is critical. The Redwood-70B-distill gave the highest quality but at higher cost; use it for critical reranking workloads only.

Performance snapshot (on Redwood-hosted test pool, single-region, approx. t3-like latency nodes):
- Mistral-7B-v2: TPS 180 req/s, p50 78ms, p95 310ms
- Llama-3-13B (INT4): TPS 250 req/s, p50 60ms, p95 360ms
- Redwood-70B-distill: TPS 45 req/s, p50 210ms, p95 520ms

Quality notes (from eval rubric you shared):
- Mistral-7B-v2: 93.5% pass (meets your 92% bar), occasional hallucination on long-context extraction tasks.
- Llama-3-13B (INT4): 90.8% pass (minor regressions on rare corner intents; see "quality-regressions.csv" in the report).
- Redwood-70B-distill: 96.1% pass (best for reranking/high-precision use cases).

Attached: redwood_verified_profiles_qps_latency.pdf (per-model TPS, memory, latency percentiles + recommended batch/caching configs), and links to CSVs with raw evals.

Next steps / asks:
1) Marissa will follow up with a short slide (1-2) summarizing recommended deployment config and cost estimate per 1M queries / month.
2) If you want, we can run a secondary pass for the Llama-3-13B with mixed-precision (FP16) to check if quality improves vs INT4 without blowing up latency.
3) Confirm Tue 2026-03-09 10:00am PT for the review call — Alex, Marissa, Mike, Sara.

Quick note on regressions: we flagged ~18 examples where INT4 quant caused subtle label flips. We included suggested prompt repairs and guardrails in the report — happy to walk through them on the call.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_verified_profiles_qps_latency.pdf, acme_model_fit_raw_results.zip (links in Drive)
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmecorp.com>

Date: 2026-03-03T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit / evals

Thanks Alex — this is super helpful.

Two quick items:  
- Please add a bullet on recommended fallback policy in the slide (e.g., if p95 > 500ms, route to smaller Llama-3-13B INT4 with cached KV).
- We also want an explicit note on data retention for the eval pool (how long you keep raw prompts/eval logs).

We’re good to confirm Tue 2026-03-09 10:00am PT.

Sara Patel
Director, Product Ops, Acme Corp
